text: Safer business environment critical to unlock private sector growth

HÀ NỘI - Ensuring economic security, protecting property rights and safeguarding lawful business freedoms are essential to creating a safe investment environment and enabling Việt Nam's private sector to grow sustainably, heard a conference organised by the Ministry of Public Security in Hà Nội on November 16.
Lieutenant General Nguyễn Sỹ Quang, director of the ministry's Economic Security Department, said the private sector had expanded significantly after nearly four decades of economic reforms.
Politburo's Resolution No. 68-NQ/TW identifies the private sector as one of the most important drivers of the national economy.

The sector currently comprises more than 940,000 enterprises and over five million household businesses, contributes around 50 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) and more than 30 per cent of State budget revenue, and employs approximately 82 per cent of the country's workforce, Quang said.
Besides, private businesses are playing a growing role in promoting innovation, improving labour productivity and strengthening national competitiveness.
Several major private conglomerates have expanded their participation in global value chains, adopted new technologies and developed Vietnamese brands in international markets.
Quang said the country's pursuit of rapid and sustainable growth required greater mobilisation of the private sector's potential.

Under Resolution 68, the sector is expected to take a pioneering role in developing science and technology, innovation and digital transformation, in line with Politburo's Resolution No. 57-NQ/TW, as well as creating new growth drivers.
However, the expansion of private businesses also poses challenges to economic security, including commercial fraud, scams and violations involving corporate assets, data and reputation.
These risks could undermine the investment and business environment if not identified and addressed proactively.
Thus, ensuring economic security is critical to support the development of the private sector as well as the protection of national security, Quang said.

He called for focusess on protecting the legitimate rights and interests of businesses, creating a safe and transparent investment environment, mobilising social resources and strengthening business confidence.

At the conference, participants also discussed issues surrounding economic security in relation to private sector development, stressing the need to identify emerging risks early and improve the prevention and handling of violations.

Protecting property ownership, lawful business freedoms and equal access to development opportunities was identified as essential to encouraging enterprises to make long-term investments, expand operations, adopt new technologies and participate more deeply in domestic and international value chains.

It is necessary to enhance coordination between the public security forces, State management agencies, industry associations and businesses to ensure timely information sharing, early risk identification and prompt responses to emerging problems to help improve economic security and create more favourable conditions for investment, participants said.

Lieutenant General Vũ Thanh Chương, director of the Department of Public Security History, Science and Strategy, Việt Nam stressed the need to establish a transparent, equal and secure investment and business environment to enable private businesses to take the lead in growth, innovation, digital transformation and improvements in competitiveness.
Protecting property rights and lawful business freedoms should be a priority to strengthen business confidence, encourage investment expansion and unlock social resources, he said.

The public security forces should also step up efforts to prevent and combat online fraud, commercial and tax fraud, and violations of businesses' legitimate interests to protect Vietnamese brands and maintain a stable business environment.
Chương also called for further improvements in institutions and policies for private sector development. - VNS
